knowledge_point.title: Plotting a Line Using a Table

question.:question/problem:
Copy and complete the table below and use it to determine which of the following is the graph of $y=x-2.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ |  |  |  |  |
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we fill the table. Given a value of $x,$ we can find the corresponding $y$ by substituting $x$ into the formula $y=x-2.$ Therefore,

- if $x=0$ then $y=(0)-2=-2,$

- if $x=1$ then $y=(1)-2=-1,$

- if $x=2$ then $y=(2)-2=0,$ and

- if $x=3$ then $y=(3)-2=1.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We plot these $(x,y)$ pairs on the $xy$-plane:

![](images/4f/4fc0e4386dd956c2b98c844941ce2e27cd1c9ca8578aca4cf5142e6971911831.png)

Finally, connecting the points gives us a straight line. This is the graph of $y=x-2.$

![](images/89/893dba533e0afffe05f9603293355ccf38b2723fcd91608ea03fe321e26a0d5f.png)
